text:
jia: Quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline tradeoffs — thinking about moving the heavy bench (full golden/regression eval) to async post-accept, and keep the fast adapter/tokenizer checks sync at intake. Thoughts?

mike: Agree in principle. Main risk is we accept models that pass lightweight checks but fail the heavy bench later => downstream quality incidents. We need mitigations: canary traffic + auto-rollback and a clear quarantine state.

sara: Proposal: two-phase acceptance. 1) intake sync smoke: tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass, tiny perf check. 2) gated async bench: full golden + regression eval on reserved bench pool. If async fails, mark model as `quarantine` and block routing. Also need a narrow interface between intake and bench for signals.

oliver: Important note — keep a compact "fast-probe" golden set in intake (~50 inputs) to catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer encodings, padding, EOS behavior). That will reduce wasteful async runs. Bench infra should emit categorical verdicts: accept / flag / critical-fail.

jia: How should we version golden artifacts? If intake and async bench use different golden sets we risk false positives/negatives. Idea: store `golden_set_id` in model metadata and surface it to runtime & bench.

mike: +1. Also: make smoke thresholds intentionally loose; async bench enforces strict thresholds. For rollout, use shadow traffic + small canaries to validate behavior on real queries before full promotion.

sara: API contract sketch: intake returns a candidate_id. Bench polls /bench-status?candidate_id or we push a webhook. Bench status payload should include: status, failed_tests[], drift_score, latency_p95, golden_set_id. Example minimal payload:
```json
{
  "candidate_id": "cand-2026-03-01-42",
  "status": "quarantine",
  "failed_tests": ["regression:qa-v2"],
  "drift_score": "0.32",
  "latency_p95_ms": "312",
  "golden_set_id": "gold-2026-02-15-v3"
}
```

bench-bot: Bench job queued: candidate_id=cand-2026-03-01-42, estimated_gpu_hours=3, expected_completion=~6h. Status webhook will fire to intake when done.

oliver: Ops checklist: we need cost caps for async bench (max GPU-hours per org/day) and a fallback if bench never completes (e.g., pending >24h => auto-reject or require human override). Also consider prioritization queue for high-risk customers.

jia: Noted. I'll draft a short RFC with proposed API surface, lifecycle states (candidate -> accepted_pending_bench -> accepted / quarantine / rejected), and rollout recipe (shadow -> small canary -> ramp). Will include golden_set versioning + sample inputs for intake. Volunteers to review the RFC? :coffee:
mike: I'll review. :+1:
